PLTR.thesis_one_line: A software firm growing revenue 93% a year with huge profits and no debt, but the share price already assumes roughly a decade of similar growth.
kill_criteria: Revenue growth below 60% y/y in any quarter (Q2-26: 93%).
FY26 revenue guidance midpoint cut below $8.0 billion (Aug-26 midpoint: $8.154 billion).
GAAP income from operations margin below 35% in any quarter (Q2-26: 47%).
Trailing-twelve-month operating cash flow less capex below $2.5 billion (Q2-26: $3.36 billion).
Top three customers above 25% of revenue for any six-month period (H1-26: 16%).
key_adverse_facts: Price implies about 34% a year FCF-after-SBC growth for 10 years vs base 25%
Top three customers 16% of H1-26 revenue; RPO $4.9bn; most contracts terminable for convenience
SBC $836M TTM (13.6% of revenue); diluted shares 2,569M vs 2,403M basic
Effective tax rate 1.4% (NOLs under valuation allowance) and non-operating equity gains inside GAAP net income
Investee 'strategic commercial contracts' ($326M total value); some investees bankrupt or terminated
data_conflicts: Triage Q11 cited 92.8% growth and 88.8x NTM P/E; d4 shows forward P/E 81.6x (forward EPS $2.32). Filing revenue growth 93% confirmed.
d4/Yahoo shares outstanding 2,300.7M counts Class A only; 10-Q total 2,402.9M (A+B+F) used.
b1 mom_12_1 is +2.2% (35th pct); no conflict with filings.
PLTR.confidence_in_thesis: high for business quality (primary-source numbers, six straight beat-and-raise quarters); low for any return expectation because the result is dominated by the terminal growth assumption.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row. Reverse DCF implies 34% a year 10-year FCF-after-SBC growth (9% discount, 3% terminal) versus my 25% base (about $99 a share) and 12% bear (about $40); bull 35% is roughly today's price.

PLTR.scenario_basis: Start TTM FCF after SBC $2.52bn (FY26 guide adj. FCF $4.5-4.7bn less about $1.0bn SBC); FY29 FCF after SBC bear $5.5bn at 25x NTM, base $7.9bn at 45x, bull $10.4bn at 60x; net cash $19-30bn added; diluted shares 2,475M (+1%/yr); no dividend.

BXP.thesis_one_line: America's biggest premier-office landlord is slowly refilling buildings and pays a 4.4% dividend, but heavy debt and costlier refinancing leave little growth to justify the price.
kill_criteria: BXP's Share of Net Debt to BXP's Share of EBITDAre (supplemental, annualised) above 9.0x in any quarter (Q2-26: 7.94x).
Total portfolio occupancy below 86.0% in any quarter (Q2-26: 88.4%).
FY26 FFO per share guidance midpoint cut below $6.90 (Jul-26 midpoint: $7.02).
Quarterly dividend reduced below $0.70 per share.
The $2.3 billion 767 Fifth Avenue mortgage (matures 9 Jun 2027) not refinanced or extended by 31 Mar 2027.
key_adverse_facts: $1.0bn 2.750% notes due 1 Oct 2026 refinanced with $700M 6.050% notes due 2036 (about $0.13 per unit annual drag)
$2.3bn 767 Fifth Avenue mortgage (BXP 60%) matures 9 Jun 2027; $750M 6.75% notes Dec 2027, $1.0bn 4.5% Dec 2028
FAD $3.19 per unit TTM is 45% of FFO; Q1-26 FAD payout 140%
FY25 FFO $6.85 missed the $6.89-$6.92 guidance; impairments in Q3-25 (EPS -$0.77) and Q2-26
Litigation over a 2010 NYC acquisition: up to a further $25M plus interest claimed
data_conflicts: Triage cited 9.8x net debt/EBITDA; company-defined BXP-share net debt/EBITDAre is 7.94x (Q2-26 supplemental). Basis of 9.8x not reproducible.
d4 forward P/E 28.5x is GAAP EPS; FFO-based P/FFO 9.0x is the relevant multiple.
Market cap: b1 $10.1bn (159.5M shares) vs d4/Yahoo $11.5bn (includes OP units).
BXP.confidence_in_thesis: medium: leasing and guidance trends are improving and filings are clear, but the valuation answer is sensitive to refinancing rates and the cost-of-equity choice.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row. TTM FAD of $3.19 per unit implies 3.8% perpetual growth at 9% cost of equity (4.7% at 10%) versus my 3.0% base; 3-year base total return about 5.8% a year is below the cost of equity.

BXP.scenario_basis: Start 2026 FFO guide midpoint $7.02, dividend $2.80; bear FFO $6.40 at 7.0x plus $2.40 dividends; base FFO $7.40 at 9.0x plus $2.80 dividends; bull FFO $8.00 at 10.5x plus $3.00 dividends; 3 years.

MRNA.thesis_one_line: A vaccine maker with about $2bn of yearly sales and $3bn of yearly losses whose shares already assume cancer-vaccine success worth many times today's business.
kill_criteria: Year-end 2026 cash and investments below $4.5 billion (latest guide $4.7 to $5.2 billion, before the $3.0 billion convertible proceeds).
FY26 revenue below $1.9 billion (FY25: $1,944 million; target up to 10% growth).
Federal Circuit ruling against Moderna on the 28 U.S.C. 1498 appeal triggering the contingent payment of up to $1.3 billion.
INTerpath-001 Phase 3 melanoma data (ESMO, 24 Oct 2026) not showing a statistically significant event-free-survival benefit over pembrolizumab alone.
Quarterly R&D plus SG&A above $950 million (Q2-26: $867 million), excluding any settlement charge.
key_adverse_facts: Price implies about $8bn year-10 FCF (about $23bn revenue) vs my base $3bn
FY25 revenue $1,944M (-40%); 2026 target only 'up to 10%' growth; Q2-26 revenue $145M vs operating loss $815M
H1-26 operating cash flow -$1,156M; cash and investments $6.91bn at 30 Jun 2026 before $950M July settlement payment
Contingent additional Arbutus/Genevant payment up to $1.3bn depending on Federal Circuit appeal; no accrual
$3.0bn 0% convertible notes due 2032 (conversion about $210.58) plus $600M term loan: debt about $3.6bn
Norovirus Phase 3 missed early-success criteria; US flu/COVID combination awaiting FDA refiling guidance
data_conflicts: Triage Q06 said price was far off highs; price has since risen roughly 40% in September (about $134 on 31 Aug to $198.88) on melanoma data, so the triage card is stale.
d4 forward EPS -$4.47 vs current-year EPS -$8.40 reflect the $0.9bn settlement timing; filings show FY26 cost of sales guide about $1.7bn including the settlement.
FDA approval of mFLUSIVA (5 Aug 2026) is from press reports; no filing found.
MRNA.confidence_in_thesis: medium: the facts (cash, burn, revenue) are solid from filings; the outcome is dominated by binary clinical data on 24 Oct 2026 that I cannot forecast.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row. Reverse DCF needs about $8.0bn year-10 FCF (9% discount, 3% terminal) versus my base $3.0bn (about $78 a share) and bear $0 (about $6); bull $8bn equals today's price.

MRNA.scenario_basis: Start 2026 revenue about $2.1bn, underlying burn about $2bn a year, net cash about $5.4bn; bear 2029 revenue $2.0bn at 4x EV/sales (about $19/share); base $4.0bn at 10x (about $96); bull $9bn at 12x (about $252); no dividend.
